message.content: {"answer": "B", "option_text": "A homogeneous well-circumscribed opacity with an obtuse angle with the chest wall, suggesting an extrapulmonary mass such as a pleural mass.", "reason": "The lateral chest radiograph (Figure 1) demonstrates a large, homogeneous, well-circumscribed opacity in the posterior right hemithorax. The mass forms an obtuse angle with the chest wall/posterior structures, which is the classic radiographic sign of an extrapulmonary (pleural or chest wall) origin rather than an intrapulmonary lesion. This finding is corroborated by the axial CT images (Figures 2 and 3), which confirm a large, homogeneous soft-tissue mass arising from the pleura/chest wall without air bronchograms."}
